tagline: Once the greatest city of Islamic Spain, Córdoba is famous for the Mezquita, a mosque-cathedral of striped arches, a Roman bridge and flower-filled patios.
overview: Córdoba, on the Guadalquivir River in Andalusia, was the capital of the Caliphate of Córdoba in the 10th century and one of the largest, most learned cities in Europe. Muslims, Christians and Jews lived and worked here, and its scholars included the philosophers Averroes and Maimonides.

Its great monument is the Mezquita, a mosque begun in 785 with a forest of red-and-white striped arches; after 1236 it became a cathedral, and a Renaissance nave was built in its centre. The Roman Bridge leads to it across the river, and the historic centre is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

The Judería, the old Jewish quarter, has a medieval synagogue and narrow white lanes. In May, the Patios Festival opens private courtyards covered in flowerpots to visitors, and the Alcázar de los Reyes Cristianos has terraced gardens and Roman mosaics. Medina Azahara, a ruined caliphal city, lies just outside town.

funFacts.title: A CALIPH'S CAPITAL
funFacts.text: Córdoba was capital of the Caliphate of Córdoba in the 900s.

funFacts.title: A FOREST OF ARCHES
funFacts.text: The Mezquita has more than 800 columns.

funFacts.title: A CATHEDRAL INSIDE A MOSQUE
funFacts.text: A Renaissance cathedral was built in the Mezquita's centre in the 1500s.

funFacts.title: ROMAN ROOTS
funFacts.text: Córdoba's Roman Bridge dates back to the 1st century BC.

funFacts.title: GREAT THINKERS
funFacts.text: Averroes and Maimonides were born in Córdoba.

funFacts.title: SENECA'S CITY
funFacts.text: The Roman philosopher Seneca was born here.

funFacts.title: FOUR UNESCO LISTINGS
funFacts.text: The Mezquita, historic centre, Patios Festival and Medina Azahara are UNESCO-listed.

funFacts.title: FLOWER PATIOS
funFacts.text: The May Patios Festival is a UNESCO intangible heritage.

funFacts.title: SALMOREJO
funFacts.text: Córdoba's thick cold tomato soup is salmorejo.

funFacts.title: HOT SUMMERS
funFacts.text: Córdoba is one of the hottest cities in Europe in summer.
